quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and stay straight. Only brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use your high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: A rider is well-protected by wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding; the wobble will likely stop.
Brake quickly.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Accelerate quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can and fix the problem.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane positions to choose from. The safest position depends on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana begins to affect you within minutes and effects last two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to begin working but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.
In any part of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right part of the lane. Be ready to change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: Acceleration may be faster, but stopping takes longer.
Both acceleration and stopping take longer.
Acceleration takes longer, but stopping is faster.
Both acceleration and stopping are faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both acceleration and stopping take longer.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and longer to stop.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass when you can do so safely. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What should a group do if one rider wants to go faster than the others?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
Speed up to accommodate the one rider.
Split up and have every rider travel at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one member wants to ride faster than the others, let them go ahead. Meet at a designated spot later.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Increase your speed to exit the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep going straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be visible to others. Orange, red, yellow, and green clothing work best.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle discouraged?

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and helps them see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: Which clothing choice is not good for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Gloves made of leather
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide proper protection.

questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used properly.
Yes, even if used improperly.
Only if the rear brake fails.
No, it should not be used regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of the total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or with mechanical turn signals. Extend your left arm straight out to the left to signal a left turn or lane change to the left.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handlebars.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. You should not have to stretch to reach the handlebars, and your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Look at it carefully for damage.
Get a new one.
Give it to another rider.
Put a new chinstrap on it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a new one.
questions.explanation: Always get a new helmet after a crash. A helmet that has been in a crash may be damaged and will not protect you properly.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When should you stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: When the road is dry.
When conditions are normal.
When the road is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead when the road is wet. You need more space to stop safely. Also increase your distance in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: A dog is chasing you while you ride. What should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for the dog to leave.
Turn sharply to avoid the dog.
Slow down and approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, shift to a lower gear and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate to leave it behind.

questions.question: When riding on a rough surface, how should you hold the handgrips?

options.text: Hold them loosely so the bike can move freely.
Hold them firmly to stay in control.
Use full throttle to power through the rough area.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, grip the handgrips firmly. This keeps your motorcycle pointed in the right direction and gives you better control.
